summary.text: A 19-year-old Chinese female active cheerleader somersaulted in mid-air on a trampoline, landed on her feet with her knees slightly flexed and felt immediate excruciating pain. She could not stand independently and was brought to the emergency department by ambulance, then admitted. She had no past medical history, no family history of connective tissue disorders, and no previous prolonged antibiotic or steroid usage.

Examination of both knees showed effusions, proximally migrated patellae, significant infrapatellar tenderness, loss of active knee extension and a palpable gap in both patella tendons. Radiographs showed bilateral patella alta and MRI scans showed complete rupture of bilateral patellar tendons.

She underwent bilateral patella tendon rupture repair with internal brace. Both retinacula were torn and the ruptured tendons were narrow and thin. The right knee had a transosseous repair of the distal stump after the proximal stump was excised, augmented with a box internal brace construct; the left knee had direct Krakow suture tape repair with internal brace augmentation, and retinacula were repaired.

Postoperatively she wore bilateral knee braces locked in extension for 2 weeks, was reviewed every 2 weeks up to 2 months with progressive flexion, and had physiotherapy up to a year. She reached 0° to 100° at 3 months and the braces were removed, walked without a limp at 5 months, and had 0° to 130° with restored quadriceps bulk at 12 months. At last review 2.5 years after surgery she had excellent outcomes and had returned to hiking and jogging.
